articles.description: Win over El Salvador would qualify US for Brazil 2027 Naomi Girma misses squad due to injury Sam Coffey returns after injury absence In the two years since the Paris Olympics, Emma Hayes has thoroughly tested fresh faces and new combinations, gathering a considerable amount of data about the US women’s national team. It’s been a thorough process, with 33 players earning their first caps since Hayes assumed the post, to bring her roster of options to 61 players. At last, the main event is nearing. On Black Friday, the United States will enter the Concacaf W Championship with a clear objective: beat El Salvador. Winning the whole thing is nice, of course, and the USWNT have done so in nine of its 11 installments to date. But by far the most important game on that journey is the first one, a 27 November quarter-final date with clear stakes: overcome El Salvador or rely on a playoff to reach next summer’s World Cup. articles.dek: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry…
articles.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

articles.description: Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career “I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds. Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. articles.dek: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s…
articles.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team? ” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles.

And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. articles.description: Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall score in first half US advance to Nations League finals 8-0 on aggregate Mauricio Pochettino departs to take over Man United The US men’s national team is through to the semi-final of the Concacaf Nations League, following Saturday’s 6-0 romp with a workmanlike 2-0 win over Haiti in the Cincinnati-hosted second leg. Towering 19-year-old center back Neil Pierre was cap-tied to the US with an appearance, eliminating the potential for him to represent Haiti in future windows.
